$comment: TF-C96 D-CSUBSET-DARWIN-BSD-STRUCT-BY-NAME — `struct itimerval` shipped by the <sys/time.h> descriptor as TWO BY-VALUE `struct timeval` members, the shape sqlite's test1.c + mem1.c needed. A descriptor SHADOWS the real header, so a name it omits is simply MISSING: `struct itimerval` (SDK sys/time.h:92) was absent, xnu's `struct extern_proc` embeds one BY VALUE so extern_proc stayed incomplete, and that made `kinfo_proc`'s kp_proc a second incomplete member — 4 `S0026` from that ONE hole. Nesting by NAME (both members spell the bare tag `timeval`) is what lets itimerval need no per-format `variants` of its own: the reference resolves to whichever timeval variant this target selected, so the one place a tv_usec width is stated stays the timeval entry. MEASURED NATIVELY on arm64 Darwin with Apple clang: sizeof(struct itimerval)==32, it_interval@0, it_value@16; sizeof(struct timeval)==16, tv_sec 8 bytes @0, tv_usec 4 bytes @8. Every one is re-derived at RUNTIME — `sizeof` on the objects, offsets by pointer arithmetic on a real `struct itimerval` — not restated as a constant. TWO INDEPENDENT RISKS, each with its own pin because neither can see the other's failure: (1) the OUTER shape is DERIVED — the descriptor spells both members as the bare tag `timeval`, so dropping `it_interval` or re-spelling either as a POINTER MOVES the offsets, which the pointer-arithmetic offsets catch; (2) the INNER width is INVISIBLE to (1) — an inner timeval with a stale i64 tv_usec still totals 16, so sizeof stays 32 and the offsets stay 0/16, NO offset anywhere moves, and what breaks is the VALUE (a read folds 4 undefined padding bytes into tv_usec's high half, a write clobbers them) in every by-value nest: xnu sys/proc.h:122 embeds one as `struct extern_proc`'s p_realtimer, and sys/sysctl.h:473 embeds THAT as `kinfo_proc`'s kp_proc. Hence the INNER pins: sizeof(tv_usec)==4 plus a byte-level STORE witness — poison bytes 28..31 (the inner struct's trailing pad), store tv_usec, and an i32 store leaves them intact where a stale i64 store erases them. Both nested timevals are written and read back so the inner struct is materialized, not merely named. NO setitimer/getitimer call — the descriptor ships the TYPE and no such symbol. exit = it_value's offset (16) + tv_usec's offset inside it (8) + sizeof(struct timeval) (16) + it_value.tv_sec read back after a runtime store of the mutable global g_secs (2) = 42. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete the `itimerval` row from the shipped <sys/time.h> descriptor -> the struct is not injected and test1.c's original `S0026` returns -> no binary; re-spell either member as a POINTER or drop it_interval -> the offset guard returns 6; regress the inner tv_usec to i64 -> the width guard returns 4 and the padding-survival witness returns 9. Single arm64-macho target -> the macos-latest CI leg; the release arm runs the optimizer over the folded sizes, the byte stores and the nested member accesses. clang -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra cross-checked clean at -O0 and -O2, same source exits 42.
